display.purpose: One high-level statement before the setup flow.

label.purpose: Compact state and data labels, not long prose.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Hover and focus response on controls only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable transitions and smooth scrolling when requested.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Owner-wallet transactions such as create and save.

components.name: Top Navigation
components.description: Owner and chain are visible before transactions.

components.name: State Pill
components.description: Text-first state indicator; never color alone.

components.description: One editable rule with a visible order and no shadow.

components.name: Service Boundary

components.html:
Service access is separate.

A service applies its own resource permissions.

narrative.overview: A technical operator uses this interface to configure one smart account. Restrained surfaces and familiar controls keep chain state, ownership, signer authority, and policy actions inspectable. It rejects generic SaaS dashboard cards, faux-glass crypto styling, dense wallet jargon without explanation, and decorative graphics that obscure the setup sequence.
keyCharacteristics: A numbered setup flow because order is operationally meaningful.
Exact addresses and hashes in mono, with plain-language labels beside them.
Read-only checks and wallet transactions use visibly different action treatments.
Service resource authorization is explained separately from account execution policy.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Keep #006d66 for actions and confirmed state, not decorative fills.

rules.name: The Data Is Not a Headline Rule
rules.body: Addresses and hashes wrap safely in compact mono text; they never determine the page's visual hierarchy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Do not combine wide soft shadows with bordered panels. State changes use color and text, not simulated floating layers.

dos: Do distinguish read-only verification from owner-wallet transactions through label and button treatment.
Do show exact agent, owner, validator, hook, and EntryPoint addresses after verification.
Do preserve 4.5:1 body contrast, visible keyboard focus, text status, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep new setup screens within this single-agent workflow unless the product scope changes.
donts: Don't use generic SaaS dashboard cards or hero metrics.
Don't use faux-glass crypto styling or purple/neon gradients.
Don't introduce dense wallet jargon without explanation near the relevant action.
Don't add decorative graphics that obscure the setup sequence.
Don't imply that onchain execution policy grants service API access.
